_comment: Deployment template for Huaxin Tool settings.
Copy this file next to the executable and rename it to
settings.template.json. On first run, any machine with no settings file of
its own starts from this one - which is how an organisation ships the same
timeouts, log level and policy to every workstation.
A user's own settings, once saved, always win. This file is a starting
Every key here is optional. Omit what you do not want to set, and remove
this _comment block if you prefer - the loader ignores keys it does not
_comment_logging: log_level: debug, info, warning, error, critical.
log_file: leave empty to write flash_log.txt beside the executable.
log_max_bytes: the log rotates to a single .1 backup past this size.
save_logs_automatically keeps one copy per session under sessions/.
_comment_timeouts: Seconds. The transfer timeout is separate from the command timeout because
a multi-gigabyte image over a marginal hub legitimately takes minutes.
_comment_retries: attempts includes the first, so 1 disables retrying. Delays are in
milliseconds and double each attempt up to retry_max_delay_ms.
Only failures that could plausibly succeed on a second try are repeated: a
failed write and a locked bootloader never are.
_comment_behaviour: confirm_destructive_operations is the one setting worth thinking hard about
before turning off in a deployment: it is the only thing standing between a
speed_limit is bytes per second; 0 means no cap. It exists for marginal links
that enumerate fine and then fail under sustained load.
theme: midnight, graphite or daylight. Daylight exists for a bench with a
window behind it, where a dark interface is genuinely hard to read.
